mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing lost control with Morris's ideal was most worthwhile: it made enjoyable, useful work a concrete alternative without presenting it as a complete economic solution.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final machine comparison felt somewhat repetitive after the initial discussion of lost control, although it clarified the distinction between effort and autonomy.

surprise.text: The distinction between saving labour and giving workers more control sharpened my understanding; one does not guarantee the other.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the first was the only offered combination and its connection to Marx's critique was not fully apparent beforehand.

continue.text: I would continue: the comparison of competing ideas about work was useful, even if the compatible choices made the outcomes fairly predictable.
